Illinois.notes: Illinois land trusts (Chicago Title Insurance Co. type) have NO enabling land-trust statute: they rest on common law (Claflin v. Bosson / Chicago Title & Trust practice) plus the Illinois Trust Code (760 ILCS 3) as general trust law. Per task instruction, entry cites the Illinois Trust Code creation

sources.title: Fla. Stat. § 689.071 (Florida Land Trust Act, ch. 689 part X)

Florida.notes: The Florida Land Trust Act is Fla. Stat. ch. 689, part X, § 689.071 et seq. (§§ 689.071-689.0717). Florida Senate hosts the official statute text; section number and act name match on-page.

sources.title: Ind. Code § 30-4-2-13 (Application of statute of uses — preserves trustee title where beneficiary directs sale)

Indiana.notes: Indiana has no statute named 'land trust'; its land-trust recognition basis is IC 30-4-2-13 (Statute of Uses does not defeat trustee title when the beneficiary controls sale — the classic Illinois-type land-trust structure). IC 30-4-2-9 dropped from citations after independent check could not verify its text against the official source.

sources.title: Va. Code § 55.1-117 (Land trusts not to fail because no beneficiaries are specified by name and no duties laid on trustee; when interest of beneficiaries deemed personal property; liens)

Virginia.notes: This is the Virginia land trust statute (former § 55-17.1, recodified to Title 55.1 § 55.1-117). Distinct from § 55.1-1200 (community land trust definition in landlord-tenant law) — do not confuse the two.

sources.title: Ohio R.C. § 5301.255 (Memorandum of trust recording for conveyances by trustee of a disclosed trust)

Ohio.notes: Ohio has no statute named 'land trust'. Its land-trust recognition basis is general trust law plus R.C. 5301.255, which expressly accommodates trustee-titled real-property conveyances via a recordable memorandum of trust (the Illinois-type deed-to-trustee mechanism). Historical connection: R.C. 1707

California.notes: California does NOT specifically authorize/recognize Illinois-type land trusts: there is no land-trust statute in the Probate Code (index contains zero 'land trust' provisions); trusts holding real property ride on general Division 9 Trust Law (§§ 15200-15212 creation chapter). california.public.law
